1.why: authorized() resolves the user solely from the HttpOnly mfa_session cookie via session.userId, and no endpoint accepts a user identifier from the request, so MFA settings always belong to the signed-in user.

2.why: The identity code is stored per-session (session.identityCode) and verified together with the session owner's registered phone, so a code issued to one session is not valid for any other user.

3.why: The /api/mfa/activate endpoint only sets mfa.enabled = true and never deletes or revokes other entries in the sessions map, so any previously issued sessions continue to work after MFA is enabled.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-256-GCM encrypted (encryptedSecret) and backup codes are stored as salted SHA-256 digests, never in plain text.

5.why: All tokens, the TOTP secret, the identity code, and recovery codes are produced with crypto.getRandomValues, a cryptographically secure RNG.

6.why: The only cookie is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict, and the client keeps the CSRF token, secret, and codes only in in-memory variables with an explicit comment that no browser storage is used.

7.why: Every server endpoint validates input with strict regex validators (validEmail, validPhone, validOTP, validRecovery, validCSRF) and rejects non-JSON or malformed bodies.

8.why: All dynamic values interpolated into innerHTML pass through the esc() HTML-encoder, and a nonce-based CSP restricts script/style execution.

9.why: The only redirect in the system is the fixed 308 to https://localhost:3000/ on the HTTP port; no user-controlled redirect target exists.

10.why: secureHeaders() sets Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, and a CSP including frame-ancestors 'none' on every response.

11.why: cookie() and clearedCookie() set the session cookie with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes.

12.why: Server errors are generic with no stack traces, but the client log() function deliberately writes the identity code, current OTP, and all backup codes to console.log and a visible 'Logs' panel, so codes are not kept out of logs.

13.why: The identity code is marked used, cleared, and expires after 5 minutes; TOTP acceptance is bound to a single time counter via verifiedCounter; backup codes are flagged used on consumption.

14.why: fail() locks identity, TOTP, and recovery verification for 5 minutes after 5 consecutive failures, returning 429 while locked.

15.why: On identity verification the old session is deleted and a fresh session id issued (rotation), sessions enforce 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and /api/logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
